intent: A line and an arc: the Equator draws itself as a dashed yellow line on the reveal and the river draws over it, north then south, so the crossing is seen rather than said. A boat then rides the whole arc, a depth counter runs down to 220 while the river line pulses, and the two-capitals beat pins the closest pair of capitals facing each other across the water.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which river crosses the Equator TWICE?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which river crosses the Equator twice?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The Congo. It bends north over the Equator, then swings back south across it on the way to the sea.

lines.direction: hold on the basin with the line and the river both drawn; the Brazilian flag-ball thinks on 'Amazon'; an Egyptian flag-ball joins on 'Nile'; the two crossing tags land on 'arc' as the river line re-draws over the Equator
lines.text: The Amazon stays just south of the line. The Nile never gets near it. Only this river makes the arc.

lines.direction: push in toward the lower river as the stem re-draws; the depth counter runs up to 220 on 'deepest' while an anchor sticker drops; a wave sticker on 'places'
lines.text: It is also the deepest river on Earth, over 220 metres down in places.

lines.direction: tighten on the pool where the river widens; the two capital pins land on 'capitals', one each side; the 2 CAPITALS card on 'across' with an eyes sticker; the Congolese flag-ball grins on 'closest'; both pins leave at the end
lines.text: Near its end, a pair of capitals stare at each other across the water, the closest in the world.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Over the line and back. Follow us.
